title: Prop model shrinkage under the TOI-band prior: stronger pull toward the prior for goals, assists, points and PP points (one pre-declared candidate, holdout rule)
declared_before: any scoring of the candidate on 2025-26 or 2026-27. The code that builds the candidate arm and scores it (prop_model.SHRINK, the struct_cal_k2 arm, tools/backtest_props.py --arms ... --question props_shrink) is written after this file is committed. Done before this file: the exploratory dev sweep listed under prior_knowledge (2023-24 and 2024-25 only).
question: props_shrink: the live arm (struct_cal) regresses each player's per-minute rate toward the rate of his position and expected-TOI band with weights (K_MINUTES, K_PPP_GAMES) that were tuned on 2025-26 for the old pooled position prior. With the band prior the model over-weights a player's own history in goals, assists, points and PP points. Should the published fair prices use larger weights for those four stats?

prior_knowledge.statement: K re-tuning was out of scope of prereg_props_calib.json. On 2026-11-23 an exploratory session looked at the dev seasons only (2023-24, 2024-25; frames [S-1, S], history from 2022-23). 2025-26 and 2026-27 rows were not loaded by any of it. The candidate's constants were chosen from that sweep, so the dev numbers below are in-sample for the choice; the holdout is the test.
prior_knowledge.how_found: A Poisson regression of assists on log(shrunk own assist rate / band prior), offset log(lam_assists), fitted on one dev season and scored on the other, gave a coefficient of -0.24 in both directions (1+ assist log loss -0.00046, SE 0.00011): deviations from the band prior are overstated.
prior_knowledge.sweep: Every K multiplied by one factor in {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6} (each market depends on one stat's K, so these are independent per-stat sweeps); arm struct_cal; 94,445 graded regular-season player-games; log loss difference vs factor 1, SE clustered by game date.

sweep_result_struct_cal.sog15_sog25_sog35: best factor 1 to 2, differences within 0.00012 of zero: shots K left alone

prior_knowledge.candidate_on_dev_in_sample: M difference vs struct_cal -0.000234 (SE 0.000036); with each market's factor picked on one dev season and scored on the other -0.000233 (SE 0.000042; 2023-24 -0.000261, 2024-25 -0.000206).
prior_knowledge.scale: struct_cal vs base on the same dev rows was -0.00061 (prereg_props_calib_dev.json).

arms.REF: struct_cal as published since 2026-10-14 (prop_model at 625c9e95d): prior='toi_band', walk-forward logit shift, K_MINUTES shots 100 / goals 450 / assists 250 / points 200, K_PPP_GAMES 6.
arms.CAND: struct_cal_k2: REF with K_MINUTES goals 900, assists 750, points 400 and K_PPP_GAMES 12; shots 100 unchanged. Same prior, same shift procedure fitted on the candidate's own predictions (window, V0 and minimum unchanged). Nothing else changes (HALF_LIFE, TOI_HALF_LIFE, TEAM_HALF_LIFE, NB_SIZE, CONTEXT_POWER, bands).

data.frames: as prereg_props_calib.json: for target season S, pregame_features on the regular-season logs of S-1 and S (season file when it exists, else that season's rows of nhl_historical_skater_games.csv). Shift windows at the start of S reach into S-1 rows priced from the [S-2, S-1] frame.
data.lookahead: league priors (toi_band_rates) and the league goal / shot means of the context term use the whole frame, identical for both arms (accepted as negligible in prereg_props_calib.json).
data.rows: primary: every regular-season player-game with a result in the period, from opening night, whatever the number of previous games. The legacy subset (from Nov 15, >= 10 previous games) is a secondary on dev.
data.markets: the 8 prop_model.PROPS: sog15, sog25, sog35, atg, a1, p1, p2, ppp1; outcome y = 1 if the count >= threshold

split.dev: 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons. In-sample for the candidate's constants (see prior_knowledge); scored again by the tool and written to prereg_props_shrink_dev.json for the record.
split.holdout: H1 = 2025-26 regular season (the rule). H2 = every graded 2026-27 regular-season player-game through the day before the look (reported next to H1, not part of the rule: about five weeks).
split.caveat: 2025-26 is the season REF's constants were tuned on (under the position prior), which favours REF. REF's own 2025-26 numbers are public (prereg_props_calib_holdout.json); the candidate has never been scored there. 2026-27 has never been scored for this question.

metrics.primary: M = (1/8) sum over markets of mean per-row log loss (p clipped to [1e-4, 1 - 1e-4]); d_i = (1/8) sum_m (LL_CAND,m,i - LL_REF,m,i); mean d with a standard error clustered by game date. Negative favours the candidate.
metrics.secondary: per-market log loss difference with date-clustered SEs; per-market calibration ratio (mean p / observed hit rate); Brier; ratios by previous-games bucket and expected-TOI band; the shift path.

selection_and_promotion.selection: one candidate, fixed above. It goes to the holdout only if the tool's pooled dev d (CAND - REF) is < 0 with |d| >= 1 date-clustered SE; otherwise REF stays and no look is taken.
selection_and_promotion.pass: CAND replaces REF iff (1) H1 mean d(CAND - REF) < 0 (strictly), AND (2) no market's H1 log loss difference CAND - REF exceeds +2 of its date-clustered SEs. H2 and every secondary are reported whatever they are.
selection_and_promotion.holdout_look: one look, the owner's call (given 2026-11-23), only after prereg_props_shrink_dev.json is written; logged in pipeline/tools/out/props_look_log.jsonl with question = 'props_shrink' (a 'started' line before scoring); the code refuses a second look. Only REF and CAND are scored.
selection_and_promotion.if_pass: prop_model.DEFAULT_ARM = 'struct_cal_k2'; repository variable PONYXG_PROP_ARM=struct_cal rolls back.
selection_and_promotion.if_fail: nothing changes in the published path; the arm stays available behind PONYXG_PROP_ARM.

not_in_scope: shots K, HALF_LIFE / TOI_HALF_LIFE / NB_SIZE / CONTEXT_POWER re-tuning, finer K values than the declared ones, an on-ice goals-for term (exploratory dev: 1+ assist -0.00013, SE 0.00006, before this change), goal-replay tracking data.
